backgroundEn: This original beginner text describes a class weather diary. It also shows why a short record cannot tell us everything about a place’s weather.

paragraphs.en: Our class kept a weather notebook for one month. Every morning, two students looked outside before the first lesson. They wrote the date and the weather on a new page.
We used simple words: sunny, cloudy, rainy and windy. Sometimes we needed two words for the same morning. We also wrote down any changes that we saw at lunch.
At the end of the month, we counted the rainy mornings. There were more than we expected. One student said that our town was always wet. Our teacher asked us to think again.

We only had notes for one month. The next month might be different. We needed more records before we could say what the weather was usually like. We decided to keep the notebook for the rest of the school year.
